<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest income increased $273,000 from $726,000 for the year 2013 to $999,000 for the year 2014.&#160; This increase in total noninterest income resulted primarily from a gain on the sale of securities of $108,000 in 2014 and increased service charges on deposit accounts, which resulted in income of $650,000 for 2014, as compared to $542,000 for the same period of 2013. This increase in service charges is largely attributable to the deposit accounts added due to the merger with Liberty Savings Bank F.S.B., Pottsville, PA, which was completed in the first quarter of 2014.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB&#146;s efficiency ratio was 72.7% and 55.3% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.&#160; The efficiency ratio represents the percentage of one dollar of expense required to be incurred to earn a full dollar of revenue and is computed by dividing noninterest expense by the sum of net interest income and noninterest income. Based on this calculation, GNB spent $0.73 on average to earn $1.00 of revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaries and employees benefits increased $424,000, or 20.6%, for the year 2014 to $2,484,000, compared to $2,060,000 for the same period of 2013.&#160; This increase is primarily attributed to the increase in full-time equivalent employees from 30 at December&nbsp;31, 2013, to 40 at December&nbsp;31, 2014, and due mainly to the employees acquired through the merger with Liberty Savings Bank F.S.B.&#160; Occupancy and equipment expenses also increased as a result of the additional office acquired in the Liberty acquisition.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Provision for income taxes.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The provision for income taxes increased $51,000, or 5.5%, to $974,000 for the year of 2014, as compared to $923,000 for the same period of 2013.&#160; This increase is due to an increase in taxable income associated with non-deductible merger expenses incurred in 2014.&#160; The effective tax rate for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, was 40.3%, compared to 30.0% for the same period of 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Results of Operations for Fiscal Years Ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;GNB reported net income available to common stockholders of $2.2 million and $2.3 million, in 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; Basic and diluted earnings per share were $4.26 and $4.45 for 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; The decrease in net income for 2013 resulted primarily from decrease of net interest income of $200,000 and an increase of non-interest expense of $157,000 partially offset by a decrease in provision for loan losses of $36,000 and an increase in non-interest income of $90,000.&#160; Return on average assets and return on average equity for 2013 were 1.16% and 8.52%, respectively, as compared to 1.26% and 9.47% for 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Average Balance Sheet and Yield/Rate Analysis.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The following table sets forth, for the periods indicated, information concerning the total dollar amounts of interest income from interest-earning assets and the resultant average yields, the total dollar amounts of interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities and the resultant average costs, net interest income, interest rate spread, and the net interest margin earned on average interest-earning assets. For purposes of this table, average balances are calculated using monthly averages, and the average loan balances include nonaccrual loans and exclude the allowance for loan losses and interest income includes accretion of net deferred loan fees. Yields on tax-exempt securities and loans (tax-exempt for federal income tax purposes) are shown on a fully tax equivalent basis utilizing a federal tax rate of 34%.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 23.05pt;text-indent:-15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)&nbsp;Interest rate spread represents the difference between the average yield on interest-earning assets and the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 23.05pt;text-indent:-15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)&nbsp;Net interest margin represents net interest income as a percentage of average interest-earning assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 23.05pt;text-indent:-15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)&nbsp;Yields are presented on a fully tax-equivalent basis using a 34% federal statutory tax rate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 23.05pt;text-indent:-15.85pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)&nbsp;Tax equivalent adjustments to the loan average yield for tax-exempt loans were $21 and $12 for the periods ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Analysis of Changes in Net Interest Income.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The following table analyzes the changes in interest income and interest expense in terms of: (1)&nbsp;changes in volume of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities and (2)&nbsp;changes in yields and rates. The table reflects the extent to which changes in interest income and interest expense are attributable to changes in rate (change in rate multiplied by prior period volume), changes in volume (changes in volume multiplied by prior period rate), and changes attributable to the combined impact of volume/rate (change in rate multiplied by change in volume). The changes attributable to the combined impact of volume/rate are allocated on a consistent basis between the volume and rate variances. Changes in interest income on securities reflect the changes in interest income on a fully tax equivalent basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">2013 Results Compared to 2012 Results</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Net interest income.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net interest income, the primary source of revenue for GNB, is determined by GNB&#146;s interest rate spread, which is defined as the difference between income on earning assets and the cost of funds supporting those assets and the relative amounts of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. Management periodically adjusts the mix of assets and liabilities, as well as the rates earned or paid on those assets and liabilities in order to manage and improve net interest income. The level of interest rates and changes in the amount and composition of interest-earning assets and liabilities affect GNB&#146;s net interest income. Net interest income decreased by $170,000, or 2.6%, to $6.3 million in 2013, compared to $6.4 million in 2012. This decrease in net interest income can be attributed to a decrease in interest income of $370,000, or 4.8%, and a decrease in interest expense of $200,000, or 17.0%. The decrease to interest expense reflects a 17 basis point decrease in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities to 0.70% in 2013 from 0.87% in 2012.&#160; Comparatively, during 2013 and 2012, loan interest income comprised 87.4% and 85.7% of interest income, and investment interest comprised 7.9% and 9.4%, respectively, of interest income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Interest income. </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest income decreased $370,000, or 4.9%, to $7.3 million for 2013, compared to $7.6 million for 2012. This decrease in interest income can be attributed to a decrease </font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">37<a name="PB_37_081124_7056"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">in interest earned on loans of $188,000 coupled with a decrease in interest earned on investment securities of $141,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest earned on loans decreased $188,000, or 2.9%, to $6.3 million for 2013, compared to $6.5 million for 2012. This decrease was attributable to a decrease in yield on the portfolio of 51 basis points to 5.48% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, as compared to 5.99% for 2012.&#160; Partially offsetting this decrease, was an increase in the average balance of loans to $116.1 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 from $109.4 million for the comparative period of 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest earned on taxable securities decreased $79,000, or 19.8%, to $321,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $400,000 for 2012. This decrease was primarily attributable to a decline in yield on the portfolio of 32 basis points to 1.64% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to 1.96% for 2012.&#160; Also contributing to this decrease was a decline in the yield of nontaxable securities as well as a decline in the average balance of these securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest income on interest bearing deposits and federal funds sold decreased $41,000 for the year ended 2013 as compared to 2012.&#160; There was a decrease in the yield from 1.66% for the year ended 2012 to 1.50% for 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Interest expense.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense decreased $200,000, or 17.0%, to $1.0 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $1.2 million for 2012. This decrease in interest expense can be attributed to decreases in interest incurred on deposits and borrowings of $178,000 and $22,000, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest incurred on deposits decreased $178,000, or 16.0%, from $1.1 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to $0.9 million for 2013. This decrease was primarily attributable to a decrease in the cost of interest-earning deposits of 15 basis points to 0.69% in 2013 from 0.84% in 2012, partially offset by an increase of $3.3 million, or 2.5%, in the average balance of interest-bearing deposits to $135.7 million for 2013 as compared to $132.4 million for 2012. Interest on borrowings with the FHLB, decreased $22,000, or 33.9%, to $43,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $65,000 for 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Provision for loan losses.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management concluded that the allowance was adequate as of December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012 based on an analysis of both quantitative and qualitative factors in GNB&#146;s test of allowance adequacy. The provision for loan losses decreased $37,000 to $55,000 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $92,000 for 2012. These provisions were part of the normal operations of GNB for 2013. As a result of the provisions for loan losses during 2013 and 2012, GNB&#146;s allowance for loan losses amounted to $1,416,000, or 1.16%, of GNB&#146;s total loan portfolio at December&nbsp;31, 2013, compared to $1,375,000, or 1.20%, at December&nbsp;31, 2012. GNB&#146;s allowance for loan losses as a percentage of non-performing loans at December&nbsp;31, 2013 and December&nbsp;31, 2012 was 360.31% and 264.93%, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Noninterest income.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The following table shows the breakdown of noninterest income for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012 (dollars in thousands).</font></p>

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14.3</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest income increased $91,000 from $635,000 for 2012 to $726,000 for 2013.&#160; The increase in total noninterest income during 2013 compared to 2012 resulted primarily from increased income on service charges on deposit accounts of $77,000, as well as an increase in tax-free earnings on bank owned life insurance of $20,000. The increase in service charges is primarily due to the increase in deposit accounts attributable to the acquisition of Liberty Savings Bank F.S.B.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest expense was $3.9 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, a $157,000, or 4.2%, increase from noninterest expense of $3.7 million for 2012.&#160; The major changes were an increase in $161,000 in professional fees, which involved some merger expenses with Liberty Savings Bank, as well as an increase of $70,000 in Pennsylvania shares tax assessed on the larger capital base in 2013 compared to 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB&#146;s efficiency ratio was 55.3% and 52.5% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; The efficiency ratio represents the percentage of one dollar of expense required to be incurred to earn a full dollar of revenue and is computed by dividing noninterest expense by the sum of net interest income and noninterest income. Based on this calculation, GNB spent $0.55 on average to earn $1.00 of revenue during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Provision for income taxes.&#160; </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The provision for income taxes decreased $79,000, or 7.9%, to $923,000 for 2013 as compared to $1,002,000 for 2012.&#160; This decrease is due to a decrease in </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Financial Condition</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General &#151; December&nbsp;31, 2014 versus December&nbsp;31, 2013</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB&#146;s total assets increased $27.2 million, or 14.8%, to $210.9 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 from $183.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013, largely due to the assets acquired in the acquisition of Liberty Savings Bank F.S.B., Pottsville, PA, which was completed in the first quarter of 2014.&#160; The increase was primarily comprised of increases in interest bearing deposits with other institutions, and net loans of $13.0 million and $21.3 million, respectively, partially offset by decreases in investment securities of $2.4 million and decreases in certificates of deposit with other banks of $4.5 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase in GNB&#146;s total assets reflects a corresponding increase in total liabilities of $26.4 million, or 16.7%, to $184.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to $158.3 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013, and an increase in total stockholders&#146; equity of $0.8 million, or 3.0%, to $26.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to $25.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase in total liabilities is primarily due to an increase in deposits of $27.3 million, or 17.6%, to $182.3 million from $155.0 million.&#160; The net increase in total stockholders&#146; equity is primarily attributed to an increase in retained earnings of $758,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General - December&nbsp;31, 2013 versus December&nbsp;31, 2012</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB&#146;s total assets increased $1.1 million, or 0.6%, to $183.7 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 from $182.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The increase was primarily comprised of increases in net loans and in bank premises of $7.3 million and $1.0 million, respectively, partially offset by a decrease in cash and cash equivalents of $6.7 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The increase in GNB&#146;s total assets reflects a corresponding increase in total stockholders&#146; equity of $800,000, or 3.2%, to $25.4 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 compared to $24.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2012. The net increase in total stockholders&#146; equity is primarily attributed to an increase in retained earnings of $1.4 million, partially offset by decreases in accumulated other comprehensive income of $382,000 and purchases of treasury stock of $301,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Investment securities available for sale.&#160; </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The investment portfolio, a portion of which is classified as available for sale, increased $2,713,000, or 15.0%, to $20.8 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to $18.1 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The primary purposes of GNB&#146;s investment portfolio are to provide a source of liquidity sufficient to meet deposit withdraws or loan funding demands, to assist in the management of interest rate risk, and to secure certain public deposits. The amortized costs and the fair value of investment securities are as follows.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were 61 positions, out of 123 total positions, that were temporarily impaired at December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; Declines in the fair value of available-for-sale securities below their cost that are deemed to be other than temporary are reflected in earnings as realized losses to the extent the impairment is related to credit losses. The amount of the impairment related to other factors is recognized in other comprehensive income. In estimating other-than-temporary impairment losses, management considers, among other things, (i)&nbsp;the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost; (ii)&nbsp;the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer; and (iii)&nbsp;whether or not GNB is more likely than not to sell the security before recovery of its cost basis.&#160;&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, management does not have the intent to sell any of the securities in the investment table and believes that it is more likely than not that GNB will not have to sell any such securities before a recovery of cost. GNB has concluded that any impairment of its investment securities portfolio is not other than temporary but is the result of interest rate changes, sector credit ratings changes, or Company-specific ratings changes that are not expected to result in the non-collection of principal and interest during the period.&#160; Management does not believe any of the securities are impaired due to reasons of credit quality. Accordingly, as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, management believes the impairments are temporary and no impairment loss has been realized in GNB&#146;s Consolidated Statement of Income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since loans typically provide higher interest yields than other types of interest-earning assets, a substantial percentage of our earning assets are invested in the loan portfolio. Average loans for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 were $133.4 million and $116.1 million, respectively. Before allowance for loan losses, total loans outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 were $143.1 million and $121.8 million, respectively.&#160; The principal component of GNB&#146;s loan portfolio is loans secured by residential real estate. Most of GNB&#146;s real estate loans are secured by residential or commercial property.&#160; GNB does originate traditional long-term residential mortgages.&#160; GNB obtains a security interest in real estate whenever possible, in addition to any other available collateral. This collateral is taken to increase the likelihood of the ultimate repayment of the loan. Generally, GNB limits the loan-to-value ratio on loans we make to 80%. We attempt to maintain a relatively diversified loan portfolio to help reduce the risk inherent in concentration in certain types of collateral.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Allowance for loan losses.&#160; </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The allowance for loan losses represents the amount which management estimates is adequate to provide for probable losses inherent in its loan portfolio.&#160; The allowance method is used in providing for loan losses.&#160; Accordingly, all loan losses are charged to the allowance, and all recoveries are credited to it.&#160; The allowance for loan losses is established through a provision for loan losses which is charged to operations.&#160; The provision is based on management&#146;s periodic evaluation of the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses which encompasses the overall risk characteristics of the various portfolio segments, past experience with losses, the impact of economic conditions on borrowers, and other relevant factors.&#160; The estimates used in determining the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses, including the amounts and timing of future cash flows expected on impaired loans, are particularly susceptible to significant change in the near term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the allowance for loan losses was $1,158,000 and $1,416,000, respectively, or 0.81% and 1.16% of total loans, respectively.&#160; The slight decrease in the allowance for loan losses reflects a similar decrease in specific reserves on impaired loans.&#160; GNB had net charge-offs of $28,000 in 2014 as compared to net charge-offs in 2013 of $14,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table summarizes the activity related to GNB&#146;s allowance for loan losses for the five years ended December&nbsp;31:</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, nonperforming assets were approximately $991,000, or 0.47%, of total assets and nonperforming loans were 0.69% of total loans.&#160; Comparatively, at December&nbsp;31, 2013, nonperforming assets were $465,000, or 0.25%, of total assets and nonperforming loans were 0.32% of total loans.&#160; Comparatively, at December&nbsp;31, 2012, nonperforming assets were $519,000, or 0.28%, of total assets and nonperforming loans were 0.45% of total loans. Nonaccrual</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">47<a name="PB_47_075534_141"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">loans increased $598,000 to $991,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2014, from $393,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; Nonaccrual loans decreased by $126,000 to $393,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2013, from $519,000 at December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; This increase in nonaccrual loans in 2014 was primarily due to the addition of nonaccrual residential real estate loans through the acquisition of Liberty Savings Bank of Pottsville. The amount of foregone interest income on nonaccrual loans for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, was approximately $46,000 and $25,000,&#160;&#160; respectively.&#160; The increase in nonperforming assets is primarily due to loans acquired in the Liberty Savings Bank, F.S.B. merger for which specific credit marks of approximately $148,000 were recognized.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, there were approximately $455,000 of acquired loans that were on nonaccrual status since acquisition.&#160; There were no loans delinquent 90 days or greater and still accruing.&#160; For all other loans that did not exhibit evidence of deteriorated credit quality at acquisition, such loans continue to be classified as accruing. The changes in coverage ratio are illustrated in the table above.&#160; The coverage ratio is shown both including and excluding acquired loans.&#160; Management is actively monitoring and working through the non-performing loans that were acquired through merger.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The allowance for loan losses to nonperforming loans ratio is a credit metric that management utilizes in managing its asset quality.&#160; This measurement has been impacted through the acquisition of loans from Liberty Savings Bank of Pottsville during 2014 and currently stands at 116.85%.&#160; However, excluding these acquired loans, the allowance for loan losses to nonperforming loans ratio was 303.94% at December&nbsp;31, 2014, and has continued to reflect improvement in the Company&#146;s originated asset quality over the past three years.&#160; In 2011, there were residential loans of approximately $1.1 million that were on nonaccrual, which were subsequently repaid.&#160; These positive trends, along with successful ongoing problem credit resolution efforts and an improving economy, have contributed to management&#146;s overall evaluation of the adequacy of the Company&#146;s allowance for loan losses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, impaired loans totaled $1,044,000 of which none of these impaired loans had a specific allowance allocation.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, impaired loans totaled $394,000, and at December&nbsp;31, 2012, impaired loans totaled $398,000.&#160; None of the impaired loans in either year had a specific allowance allocation. Impaired loans increased in 2014 due to loans acquired in the purchase of Liberty Savings Bank, F.S.B.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, approximately 90% of our loans were collateralized by real estate, and 100% of our impaired loans were secured by real estate. GNB utilizes third-party appraisers to determine the fair value of collateral dependent loans. Impaired loans are individually reviewed on a quarterly basis to determine the level of impairment. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, there are no impaired loans carried at a value in excess of the appraised value. GNB typically records a charge-off or creates a specific reserve for impaired loans when repayment is not expected to occur as agreed upon under the original terms of the loan agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB considers a loan to be a troubled debt restructuring (&#147;TDR&#148;) when the debtor experiences financial difficulties and GNB provides concessions with the original terms of the loan agreement. Concessions can relate to the contractual interest rate, maturity date, or payment structure of the note. As part of our workout plan for individual loan relationships, GNB may restructure loan terms to assist borrowers facing challenges in the current economic environment.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

See Note 4 to the consolidated financial statements for additional information on TDRs.</font></p>

<td width="11%" valign="bottom" style="border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:11.56%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16,950</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.06%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act permanently raised the standard maximum deposit insurance amount to $250,000. The FDIC insurance coverage limit applies per depositor and per insured depository institution for each account ownership category.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Other Borrowings.&#160; </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deposits and repayment of loan principal are GNB&#146;s primary sources of funds for lending activities and other general business purposes. However, when the supply of lendable funds or funds available for general business purposes cannot satisfy the demand for loans or general business purposes, GNB can obtain funds from the FHLB. At December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, GNB had $438,000, $1,473,000, and $2,485,000 of FHLB borrowings outstanding, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Capital Resources.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Total stockholders&#146; equity was $26.2 million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 and $25.4 million and $24.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, respectively. The $800,000 increase during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, can be attributed to the other comprehensive gain in the amount of $22,000, and to net income of $1,440,000, partially offset by dividends of $682,000 during the year.&#160; The $790,000 increase during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, can be attributed to the net income of $2,151,000 partially offset by a loss in other comprehensive income of $382,000 during the year and dividends of $677,000.&#160; The $1,646,000 increase during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, can be attributed to the net income of $2,272,000 and other comprehensive income of $57,000 during the year, partially offset by dividends of $684,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table shows the return on average assets (net income divided by average total assets), return on average equity (net income divided by average equity), and equity to assets ratio (average equity divided by average total assets) for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The annualized return on average assets was 0.71% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, and for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, the return on average assets was 1.16% and 1.26%, respectively. The annualized return on average equity was 5.76% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, and for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 and 2012, the return on average equity was 8.52% and 9.47%, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Regulatory Capital.&#160; </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory, and possibly additional discretionary, actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the consolidated financial statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, GNB must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weighting and other factors. Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the maintenance of minimum amounts and ratios (as set forth in the tables below) of Total capital and Tier I capital (as defined in the regulations) to risk-weighted assets (as defined), and of Tier I capital (as defined) to average assets (as defined). Management believes that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, GNB met all capital adequacy requirements to which it is subject.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, GNB is categorized as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. To be categorized as well capitalized, GNB must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based, and Tier 1 leverage ratios as set forth in the following table (dollar figures are in thousands). There are no conditions or events since those notifications that management believes have changed those categories.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Liquidity</font></i></b><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquidity measures an organization&#146;s ability to meet its cash obligations as they come due. The consolidated statements of cash flows included in the accompanying financial statements provide analysis of GNB&#146;s cash and cash equivalents and the sources and uses of cash.&#160; Liquidity is monitored by both management and the Asset-Liability Committee, which establishes and monitors ranges of acceptable liquidity.&#160; Also, GNB is a member of FHLB which currently provides for a total borrowing capacity of approximately $84 million, with approximately $64 million, available at December&nbsp;31, 2013 and $76 million available at December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; In addition to the borrowing capacity at FHLB, the Bank has a federal funds line of $5 million with the Atlantic Central Bankers&#146; Bank.&#160; Management believes that GNB&#146;s current liquidity position is acceptable.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Market Risk and Interest Rate Sensitivity</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a financial institution, GNB&#146;s primary source of market risk is interest rate risk, which is the exposure to fluctuations in future earnings resulting from changes in interest rates.&#160; This exposure is correlated to the repricing characteristics of GNB&#146;s portfolio of assets and liabilities.&#160; Each asset or liability reprices either at maturity or during the life of the instrument.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The principal purpose of asset/liability management is to maximize current and future net interest income within acceptable levels of interest rate risk while satisfying liquidity and capital requirements.&#160; Net interest income is enhanced by increasing the net interest margin and by the growth in earning assets.&#160; As a result, the primary goal of interest rate risk management is to maintain a balance between risk and reward such that net interest income is maximized while risk is maintained at an acceptable level.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">52<a name="PB_52_081615_4141"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB uses an asset-liability management model to measure the effect of interest rate changes on its net interest income.&#160; Management also reviews asset-liability maturity gap and repricing analyses regularly.&#160; Management does not always attempt to achieve a precise match between interest sensitive assets and liabilities because it believes that an actively managed amount of interest rate risk is inherent and appropriate in the management of profitability. Asset-liability modeling techniques and simulation involve assumptions and estimates that inherently cannot be measured with precision.&#160; Key assumptions in these analyses include maturity and repricing characteristics of assets and liabilities, prepayments on amortizing assets, non-maturing deposit sensitivity, and loan and deposit pricing.&#160; These assumptions are inherently uncertain due to the timing, magnitude, and frequency of rate changes and changes in market conditions and management strategies, among other factors.&#160; However, the analyses are useful in quantifying risk and provide a relative gauge of GNB&#146;s interest rate risk position over time. Management reviews interest rate risk on a quarterly basis and reports to the Asset-Liability Committee.&#160; This review includes earnings shock scenarios whereby interest rates are immediately increased and decreased by 100, 200, 300, and 400 basis points.&#160; These scenarios, detailed in the table below, indicate that there would not be a significant variance in net interest income over a one-year period due to interest rate changes; however, actual results could vary significantly.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, all interest rate risk levels according to the model were within the tolerance limits of the Asset-Liability Committee&#146;s approved policy. In addition, the table does not take into consideration changes that management would make to realign its assets and liabilities in the event of an unexpected changing interest rate environment.&#160; Due to the historically low interest rate environment, the -200, -300, and -400 scenarios have been excluded from the table.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Effects of Inflation and Changing Prices</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The effect of relative purchasing power over time due to inflation has not been taken into account in our consolidated financial statements. Rather, our financial statements have been prepared on an historical cost basis in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of the Chief Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and the operation of GNB&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures (as such term as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, pursuant to Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15.&#160; Based upon that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer along with the Principal Financial Officer concluded that GNB&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, are effective in timely alerting them to material information relating to GNB required to be in GNB&#146;s periodic filings under the Exchange Act.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">This annual report does not include a report of management&#146;s assessment regarding internal control over financial reporting or an attestation report of the company&#146;s registered public accounting firm due to a transition period established by rules&nbsp;of the Securities and Exchange Commission for newly public companies.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Code of Ethics</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB has adopted a Code of Ethics that applies to directors and senior management of the Corporation and the Bank. The Code of Ethics is attached as Exhibit&nbsp;14 to this Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors has determined that Tammy A. Specht is qualified to serve as the GNB&#146;s audit committee financial expert and is independent as defined under applicable SEC and Nasdaq rules.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 11&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Executive Compensation</font></b><a name="Item11ExecutiveCompensation_072208"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">GNB did not compensate members of its board of directors during 2014. In 2014, the directors did receive $300 for each meeting of the Bank&#146;s board of directors that they attended.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Directors Deferred Compensation Agreements</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain GNB directors participate in the Directors Deferred Compensation Agreement, wherein the director may elect to defer a percentage and such deferral will accrue interest equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the average one year Treasury instrument for the plan year. The participants are always 100% vested in the amount they defer. The director is entitled to receive a distribution from his deferred account upon death, termination of service, or reaching age sixty-five, in the manner elected in a previously executed election form.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the Bank. The term of the agreement is three (3)&nbsp;years. In the event that Mr.&nbsp;Weymers&#146; employment is terminated without &#147;cause&#148; or the executive resigns for &#147;good reason&#148; he shall receive two times his annual base salary and life, disability, medical insurance and other normal health and welfare benefits for two (2)&nbsp;years from the termination of his employment or until he secures substantially similar benefits through other employment. If Mr.&nbsp;Weymers is involuntarily terminated without cause after a change in control of GNB or the Bank, he shall be entitled to a lump sum payment equal to 2.99 times his annual base salary and life, disability, medical insurance and other normal health and welfare benefits for 2.99 years from the termination of his employment or until he secures substantially similar benefits through other employment. In exchange for the receipt of the employment agreement and severance payments, Mr.&nbsp;Weymers is prohibited for a period of two years from the date of his termination of employment, from engaging, directly or indirectly, in the banking or financial services industry or any other activity in which GNB or the Bank are engaged in Dauphin, Northumberland, or Schuylkill counties. He is also prohibited from soliciting customers or employees of GNB or the Bank.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2013, GNB entered into an employment agreement with Aaron M. Klinger. The term of the agreement is two (2)&nbsp;years. In the event that Mr.&nbsp;Klinger&#146;s employment is terminated without &#147;cause&#148; or the executive resigns for &#147;good reason&#148; he shall receive two times his annual base salary and life, disability, medical insurance and other normal health and welfare benefits for two (2)&nbsp;years from the termination of his employment or until he secures substantially similar benefits through other employment. If Mr.&nbsp;Klinger is involuntarily terminated without cause after a change in control of GNB or the Bank, he shall be entitled to a lump sum payment equal to two times his annual base salary and life, disability, medical insurance and other normal health and welfare benefits for two (2)&nbsp;years from the termination of his employment or until he secures substantially similar benefits through other employment. In exchange for the receipt of the employment agreement and severance payments, Mr.&nbsp;Klinger is prohibited for a period of two years from the date of his termination of employment, from engaging, directly or indirectly, in the banking or financial services industry or any other activity in which GNB or the Bank are engaged in a twenty (20) mile radius of the Bank&#146;s main office. He is also prohibited from soliciting customers or employees of GNB or the Bank.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;27, 2012, the Bank and Wesley M. Weymers entered into an Executive Supplemental Retirement Plan (&#147;SERP&#148;). Under the terms of the SERP, upon Mr.&nbsp;Weymers&#146; termination of employment after retiring after the age of sixty-five and one-half (651/2), he will be entitled to an annual payment equal to $54,000 payable in equal monthly installments for fifteen (15) years. In the event that his employment is terminated prior to age sixty-five and one-half (65 1/2) including for death or disability, he will be entitled to an annual amount equal to the vested annual benefit as provided in the SERP payable in monthly installments for fifteen (15) years. If Mr.&nbsp;Weymers is terminated within twenty-four (24) months after a change in control of the Bank, he will received an annual benefit equal to $54,000 payable in equal monthly installments for fifteen (15) years. If Mr.&nbsp;Weymers is terminated for cause as defined in the agreement, he will not be entitled to any benefits under the SERP.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Wesley M. Weymers Executive Deferred Compensation Agreement</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;6, 2013, Wesley M. Weymers entered into an executive deferred compensation agreement with the Bank, which was subsequently amended. Pursuant to the agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Weymers may defer a percentage of his salary and/or bonus and such amounts will earn a rate of interest equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the average one year Treasury instrument for the plan year. Mr.&nbsp;Weymers is fully vested in the account balance and will receive payments on the first day of the calendar month following his termination of service or his sixty-fifth (65th) birthday or upon his death.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Timothy J. Allison Executive Deferred Compensation Agreement</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;8, 2002, Timothy J. Allison entered into an executive deferred compensation agreement with the Bank, which was subsequently amended. Pursuant to the agreement, Mr.&nbsp;Allison may defer a percentage of his salary and/or bonus and such amounts will earn a rate of interest equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the average one year Treasury instrument for the plan year. Mr.&nbsp;Allison is fully vested in the account balance and will receive payments on the first day of the calendar month following his termination of service or his sixty-fifth (65th) birthday or upon his death.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">GNB&#146;s Compensation Policies and Practices as they Relate to Risk Management.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The board of directors of GNB has reviewed its compensation policies and practices and has determined that the policies and practices do not motivate imprudent risk taking and are not reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on GNB.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Compensation Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No member of GNB&#146;s Salary, Pension, and Insurance Committee, which acts as its compensation committee, is or has been an officer or employee of GNB or the Bank. Also, during 2014, none of GNB&#146;s executive officers served as a member of the compensation committee. In addition, Wesley M. Weymers is an ex officio member of the compensation committee but does not participate in decisions or discussions regarding his own compensation.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 12&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters</font></b><a name="Item12SecurityOwnershipOfCertainB_072520"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Principal Holders</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table sets forth, to the best of our knowledge, those persons or entities who owned of record or beneficially more than 5% of the outstanding shares of GNB common stock as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">*</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The securities &#147;beneficially owned&#148; by an individual may include securities owned by or for the individual&#146;s spouse, minor children and any other relative who has the same home, as well as securities that the individual has or shares voting or investment power, or has the right to acquire beneficial ownership within sixty (60) days after December&nbsp;31, 2014. Beneficial ownership may be disclaimed as to certain of the securities. Unless otherwise indicated, all shares are individually owned. All numbers have been rounded to the nearest whole number.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 13&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence</font></b><a name="Item13CertainRelationshipsAndRela_073342"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Related Party Transactions</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Several of the GNB&#146;s directors, officers, their immediate family members and companies with which they are associated, are customers of the Bank. During 2014, many of them had banking transactions with the Bank, in the ordinary course of the Bank&#146;s business, and intend to do so in the future. The Bank has a formal process with respect to the review and approval of loans extended by the Bank to related persons. In accordance with these procedures all transactions with related persons must be approved or ratified by disinterested members of board of directors. All loans and commitments to loan included in such transactions were made under substantially the same terms, including interest rates, collateral, and repayment terms, as those prevailing at the time for comparable transactions with other persons not related to the lender and do not involve more than the normal risk of collection or present other unfavorable features.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Director Independence</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Currently, the GNB board of directors has eight (8)&nbsp;members. Under the Nasdaq Stock Market standards for independence, the following directors of GNB meet the standards for independence: Messrs.&nbsp;Kauffman, Koppenhaver, Masser, and Michetti and Ms.&nbsp;Specht. These directors constitute more than a majority of GNB&#146;s board of directors. Only independent directors serve on GNB&#146;s audit, nominating and compensation committees.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In determining each director&#146;s independence, the board of directors considered the services provided, loan transactions between the Bank and the director, the director&#146;s family members and businesses with whom they are associated, contributions made to non-profit organizations with whom the director is associated, and other matters that the board deemed pertinent.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fees</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> include fees billed for professional services rendered for the audit of the annual financial statements, fees billed for the review of financial statements or services that are provided by the GNB&#146;s independent accountant, in connection with statutory and regulatory filings or engagements. S.R. Snodgrass, P.C. performed all annual financial statement audit services for 2014, and Patton&nbsp;&amp; Lettich performed all annual financial statement audit services for 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tax Fees include fees billed for professional services rendered by S.R. Snodgrass, P.C., during 2014 and Patton&nbsp;&amp; Lettich during 2013, for tax compliance, tax advice, tax planning, and preparation of corporate tax returns.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All Other </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fees</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> include fees related to Bank Secrecy Act and various lending compliance audits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Audit Committee pre-approves all audit and permissible non-audit services provided by the independent auditors. These services may include audit services, audit-related services, tax services, and other services. The Audit Committee has adopted a policy for the pre-approval of services provided by the independent auditors. Under the policy, pre-approval is generally provided for up to one (1)&nbsp;year and any pre-approval is detailed as to the particular service or category of services being approved and is subject to a specific budget. In addition, the Audit Committee may also pre-approve particular services on a case-by-case basis. For each proposed service, the independent auditor is required to provide detailed back-up documentation at the time of approval.</font></p>
